newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian Sports News - Jan 23.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian Sports News - Jan 23.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

Thomas Muster advanced to the semi-finals of the Australian Open yesterday after defeating Goran Ivanisevic 6-4, 6-2, 6-3. He revealed that he had relied on a computer assessment to analyse his opponent's game and had planned his game accordingly. Page 20.

Sixteen-year-old Martina Hingis attributed her quarter final 7-5, 6-2 win in the Australian Open against Irina Spirlea to falling off a horse, she said yesterday. Hingis fell off the horse while showjumping at an equestrian centre on Tuesday and claimed that the incident had caused her to reassess her physical capabilities. Page 18.

West Indian cricket captain Courtney Walsh said that both he and fellow strike bowler Curtly Ambrose would play in the fourth Test which begins in Adelaide on Saturday. Both had been suffering from injuries and had been recuperating since the one-day finals against Pakistan in Melbourne. Page 19.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Ken Arthurson resigned last night as chairman of The Australian Rugby League. His resignation ends 50 years of involvement in the game as player, coach and official. It is believed that the resignation was sparked by last week's decision by Kerry Packer owner of Channel 9, to sign a deal with Rupert Murdoch to televise Super League games rather than ARL ones. Page 46.

Thomas Muster credited his quarter final win against Goran Ivanisevic in the Australian Open to computer analysis of the Croatian's game which cracked the riddle of his overpowering serve. Relying on the computer predictions Muster moved around the courtto the places where Ivanisevic was most likely to aim the ball and so gained 15 break points. Page 46.

Olympic champion sprinter and high jumper Carl Lewis revealed that he will concentrate on fatherhood, a film career and campaigning for political causes after he officially retires this year. Lewis is currently on his farewell world tour which includes a 100m race at Homebush Sydney Grand Prix on Monday. Page 44.
THE AGE

World No 1 Peter Sampras has won a gruelling five-set match at the Australian Open defeating Albert Costa in the quarter-finals. He will now meet Thomas Muster who defeated Goran Ivanisevic in the other quarter final. It is expected that the upcoming mach will be very hard fought. Page B8.

Swiss player, 16-year-old Martina Hingis, is being tipped to become the world's top ranked female player this year. If she does, she will beat the records established by Steffi Graf, who was 18 when she was first ranked No 1 and Monica Seles, who achieve the ranking at 17. Yesterday when she defeated Irina Spirlea she became the youngest player ever to reach a semi-final in the Australian Open. Page B7.

Veteran player Mary Joe Fernandez will today meet Martina Hingis in the semi-finals of the Australian Open. Fernandez who is ranked world No 17 is confident of her chances after beating Dominique Monami-van Roost 7-5, 4-0. Fernandez is the surprise succss of the tournament, with no-one predicting that she would achieve the semi-finals with players such as Steffi Graf and world No 2 Arantxa Sanchez Vicario competing. Page B7.
THE HERALD SUN

Batsman Matthew Elliott will return to Australian cricket this weekend, being given medical permission to play for his club Camberwell against Hawthorn-Waverley. During the Sydney Test he suffered a tear in the lateral cartilage in his right knee when hecrashed into his batting partner Mark Waugh. He hopes to be included in the team to tour South Africa to be announced on January 28. Page 80.

Former Australian cricket Test captain Greg Chappell squashed rumours yesterday that he might replace sacked Graham Halbish as Australian Cricket Board (ACB) chief executive saying that they were purely media speculation and that he had been approached byno official body. Other possible candidates for the position include ACB operations manager Richard Watson. Page 80.

Twenty-five-year-old South African Amanda Coetzer is set to play in the semi-final of the Australian Open. She is currently ranked No 14 in the world and is noted for her speed and powerful forehand. Page 82.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

Australian David Nilsson has won a four-year US$20 million contract with American baseball team the Milwaukee Brewers . He joins other Australian baseball players who have landed lucrative contracts such as Graeme Lloyd, with US$3 million, Glenn Williams US$1 million and David Balfour with US $100,000. American's are surprised at Australia producing such baseball talent when the sport is not big there, said American agent Howie Norsetter. Page 73.

The decision to close the roof at Melbourne Park, the venue of the Australian Open, has been criticised by several top players. A protest letter signed by Pete Sampras, Thomas Muster, Goran Ivanisevic, Carlos Moya and Felix Mantilla has been sent to tourament director Paul McNamee. The players are angered by the lack of consultation with them over the decision and by the fact that closing the roof turns the Open into an indoor tournament when they had trained for an outdoor one. Page 80.

The Australian Football League club Sydney Swans is considering capping its membership levels after receiving an overwhelming number of applications. The Swans are happy with the response but say they need to keep seats at matches available for the generl public. Already 50 per cent of seats at upcoming matches have been reserved. Page 75.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
